question: Can language models be trained with random SiLU/ReLU activation choices and briefly adapted to ReLU so that inference obtains high activation sparsity without the optimization and quality loss of ReLU-from-scratch training, and can the same randomness diversify generation?

key_findings.claim: Stochastic activation exposes a model to both a smooth-training and a sparse-inference regime by Bernoulli-selecting SiLU or ReLU for negative preactivations.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 3 defines the negative branch as SiLU with probability p and ReLU with probability 1-p; positive branches use either identity or SiLU. The final 5–10% activation fine-tuning switches fully to ReLU without optimizer reset or warmup.

key_findings.claim: For models trained from scratch, combining stochastic activation with a final ReLU phase closes much of the ReLU quality gap while yielding very sparse inference activations.
key_findings.evidence: On the 1.5B model, the SiLU baseline validation loss is 2.122 and ReLU-from-scratch is 2.161; stochastic activation plus final ReLU gives 2.138–2.144 for the shown p settings. The sparsity appendix reports roughly 80–90% zero activations depending on p and fine-tuning, and the downstream average is 0.451 versus 0.454 for SiLU and 0.441 for ReLU.

key_findings.claim: Measured sparsity produces hardware speedups, but the scope and headline differ between CPU end-to-end inference and GPU feed-forward kernels.
key_findings.evidence: At 90% sparsity, Figure 3 reports a 1.65x total single-token speedup on one Xeon core and about 1.5x for the GPU FFN operation; the authors explicitly note that KV-cache, masks, RoPE, Python, and other overheads dominate the small-model GPU end-to-end path.

key_findings.claim: Activation randomness increases lexical and answer diversity, but does not consistently improve answer correctness over ordinary temperature sampling.
key_findings.evidence: StochA raises type-token ratio on NQ and TQA across tested temperatures and improves selected NQ best-of-n results, but is inferior on TQA; multiple stochastic forward passes with majority-vote or maximum-probability token selection do not beat one pass.

method.core_idea: Train a decoder-only transformer under a stochastic mixture of smooth SiLU and exactly sparse ReLU behavior, then optionally spend the last fraction of pretraining in deterministic ReLU mode.
method.mechanism: A Bernoulli draw gates the negative branch of each FFN activation. The resulting model is evaluated either with ReLU for sparse inference or with stochastic activations for diverse generation; custom sparse matrix-vector kernels exploit zero gated coordinates.
assumptions: Intermittent SiLU gradients prevent the dead-neuron optimization failure associated with pure ReLU training.
A short low-learning-rate ReLU phase is sufficient to repair train/inference activation mismatch.
The hardware and batching regime can exploit unstructured activation sparsity rather than becoming overhead-bound.

techniques.role: Randomly selects smooth or sparse behavior for negative FFN preactivations during training or generation.
Uses the last 5–20% of a cosine-decay run to adapt a smooth/stochastic model to deterministic ReLU inference.
Skips memory reads and multiplications associated with zero activation coordinates at single-token inference.

evaluations.setting: Dense 1.5B- and 3B-parameter decoder-only LMs trained for about 100B and 200B tokens
evaluations.metric: Training and validation cross-entropy under SiLU, ReLU, hybrid deterministic, and stochastic activations
evaluations.result: StochA plus a final ReLU phase substantially improves over ReLU-from-scratch and approaches SiLU, while StochA without adaptation retains a ReLU test-time mismatch.
evaluations.baseline: SiLU quality topline and ReLU sparse-inference baseline.

evaluations.setting: Twelve code, commonsense, reading, math, and QA evaluations
evaluations.result: For 1.5B, StochA-plus-ReLU averages 0.451 versus 0.454 SiLU and 0.441 ReLU; for 3B it averages 0.509 versus 0.515 and 0.486.

evaluations.setting: Single-token CPU inference and H100 FFN microbenchmark at varying measured activation sparsity
evaluations.result: About 1.65x total CPU speedup and about 1.5x GPU FFN speedup at 90% sparsity.
evaluations.baseline: Dense FFN execution of the same model.

evaluations.setting: Twenty sampled answers on Natural Questions and TriviaQA
evaluations.metric: Best normalized-log-likelihood F1 and type-token ratio
evaluations.result: Stochastic activation consistently increases lexical diversity, improves some NQ best-of-n settings, and underperforms SiLU temperature sampling on TQA.

limitations: Author-stated: practical speedup depends on storage layout, sparsity-specific kernels, batch size, and overheads; sparse training itself is not accelerated.
Author-stated: stochastic generation is task-dependent and majority-vote or maximum-probability aggregation over repeated passes does not improve accuracy.
Reviewer inference: results stop at 3B parameters and a single pretraining recipe, so model-scale and architecture generalization are unestablished.
Reviewer inference: downstream averages conceal task regressions and are not paired with uncertainty or significance estimates.
failure_modes: A stochastic-to-ReLU model can preserve average benchmark score while harming tasks that rely on negative-activation information.
Unstructured zeros may yield theoretical FLOP savings but no end-to-end gain under batched GPU serving or generic dense kernels.
Changing the activation pair can fail badly: the TANH/ReLU appendix reports severe validation mismatch for some stochastic variants.
reusable_insights: Train-time randomization can continuously expose a model to an inference-time discrete approximation, analogous to quantization-aware training.
Report kernel-only and end-to-end sparse speedups separately and bind both to a concrete serving regime.
Activation noise is a controllable diversity source, but diversity and correctness require separate evaluation.
open_questions: Does the quality–sparsity frontier persist at tens or hundreds of billions of parameters and under mixture-of-experts FFNs?
Can per-layer or input-adaptive mixture probabilities dominate a global Bernoulli p?
How does stochastic activation interact with quantization, speculative decoding, batching, and long-context attention overheads?

competitive_landscape.title: ReLU Strikes Back: Exploiting Activation Sparsity in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ReLU Strikes Back trains and exploits ReLU-based LMs directly; StochA targets the remaining optimization gap by exposing one model to SiLU and ReLU and then adapting it to ReLU inference.

competitive_landscape.title: ProSparse: Introducing and Enhancing Intrinsic Activation Sparsity within Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ProSparse uses progressive sparsity regularization after replacing Swish with ReLU and reports up to 4.52x acceleration; StochA instead uses activation randomization plus a short deterministic phase and evaluates stochastic generation as a second use case.

competitive_landscape.title: Training-Free Activation Sparsity in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: TEAL prunes low-magnitude hidden activations in already trained SiLU-family models without retraining; StochA changes pretraining so exact ReLU zeros are native but requires a new training recipe.

competitive_landscape.title: Universal Properties of Activation Sparsity in Modern Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: The universal-properties study audits thresholded activation sparsity across modern and diffusion LMs; StochA proposes a specific stochastic training intervention and measures its quality, exact-zero sparsity, and hardware speed.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: Bernoulli mixing of SiLU and ReLU, optionally followed by a short ReLU phase, preserves much of SiLU's trainability while enabling exact sparse inference and a new source of generation diversity. Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: the train/test activation-mixture mechanism and paired diversity study appear distinct, but activation-sparse LLM training and deployment are crowded; the strongest novelty is the quantization-aware-style stochastic bridge, not activation sparsity or ReLU inference itself.
reviewer_notes: Read against all twenty extracted pages, including sparsity, continuous-pretraining, alternate-activation, generation, and benchmark appendices. Hardware and benchmark claims are author-reported. Scale, averaging, and serving-regime cautions are reviewer inferences. Direct competitors were checked on primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
